Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this one-sided affair where India Women takes an early lead in the series and will look to seal it in the next game while the Aussies will hope to come back stronger and level it. The 2nd T20I will be played on 7th January, Sunday at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT), but as you know, you can always join us early for all the build-up to the game. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Titas Sadhu is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for her amazing bowling performance. She says that it has been a tradition as whoever wins these awards has to give a party. Tells that as she has won all three awards, she has to give a triple part now. Adds that it has been a long tour for her and she was professional and waited for her chance and is happy to capitalise on it. Mentions that it was a good wicket to bowl on but she got a bit lucky in the second over when she got two wickets. Ends by saying that the slower ones help but there was a lot of dew in the second innings and she says they got lucky winning the toss.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the victorious skipper of India Women says that they were up to the mark in all three departments. States that fielding was something they have been working hard on and she is happy to see that they are getting the results. Credits the fielding coach for his decision to keep Jemimah Rodrigues at point looking at Australia's ability to hit square. On Litchfield's dropped catch, she says that they gave her many chances in the ODI series as well but the talk was to keep bowling in the right areas despite the error. Shares that it was a last-minute decision by the Head Coach to go in with four seamers which worked out for them. Feels that Australia will come hard at them in the next game and they will have to repeat this bowling performance.

Alyssa Healy, the captain of Australia Women says it is not ideal and they did not play very well. Tells that they left a lot out there with the bat and did not start well as well. Adds that losing early wickets did not help but losing wickets throughout also made it difficult. Mentions that normally they rely on good partnerships in the middle to set up a good total but credits the Indian bowlers for hitting the right lengths which did not let them gain momentum. Says that the side they picked for this game bat till 9, and admits it would have been handy to have an extra bowler. Ends by saying that they have to adjust to the conditions here quickly and either put up more runs on the board or change their tactics.
Presentation Time...

Smriti Mandhana is up for a quick chat. She says that she is pretty pleased with the win. Mentions that they were disappointed with the way the ODI series went. States that they were working on themselves in the last couple of days. Shares that they are really happy with the way they bowled. Further adds that from getting hit for 330-odd runs to bowling Australia out in a T20 game was a wonderful effort. Also says that they analysed what went wrong as a unit in the last couple of days and the decision to go with four seamers also helped. On Titas Sadhu's performance, she replies that she is very happy for her and Bengal has already given them a legendary cricketer in Jhulan Goswami. Adds that she does not get into comparison but Titas' work ethic and clarity are pleasing to see. Ends by saying that she remembers telling the head coach, Amol Muzumdar, to not be soft on us and to be as hard as he was during his time with the Mumbai Ranji team.

Earlier in the game, Australia Women posted a below-par total, and that too because of a couple of good knocks from Phoebe Litchfield who fell one short of her fifty while Ellyse Perry made crucial 37 runs or else they could have been bundled under 100. Titas Sadhu was the star with the ball for India with a spectacular four-fer while Shreyanka Patil and Deepti Sharma picked up a couple each. Renuka Singh and Amanjot Kaur also chipped in with a wicket each. While chasing, the Indian openers made batting look easy and the dew factor also helped them as they almost finished the job themselves, but they still finished the job losing only one wicket.

Australia Women, on the other hand, would have hoped for a better effort from their bowlers. Darcie Brown gave away 14 runs in extras in the first over from which they never really recovered. They had no answers to the onslaught of the Indian openers and were taken to the cleaners by them. They also let go of a few opportunities in the middle, but the game was long gone by then. Georgia Wareham was the only shining light for them and got the solitary wicket.

India Women got off to an absolute flier as both openers went bang bang right from the start. They were helped by the visitors giving away extras for free but once they got into their groove, there was no stopping them and they bossed the Powerplay. They continued with the same momentum throughout this chase and did not let the bowlers settle. Although both of them got a bit lucky on a couple of occasions other than that, it was easy peasy for them. They also registered the highest opening partnership for India Women against Australia Women in T20Is and in the process also notched up their respective fifties as well. Mandhana did get out on 54 trying to finish things off, but Varma stayed unbeaten on 64 and Jemimah Rodrigues hit the winning runs to register a 9-wicket win with 14 balls to spare as well.

INDIA WOMEN GO 1-0 UP IN THE SERIES! After a disappointing ODI series, this is a great comeback from the hosts. It was complete domination by the Women in Blue from the very first ball. Their bowlers set up this win while the batters made sure that their hard work did not go to waste and sealed a comprehensive victory. This is also only the second time that India Women have defeated Australia Women on home soil in this format.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and around off, Smriti Mandhana pushes it towards covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! The Indian openers are utilising the Powerplay excellently here! Darcie Brown lands this back of a length and outside off, Smriti Mandhana accepts the width on offer and crunches it past point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Darcie Brown (1-0-1-0) returns to the attack, replacing Annabel Sutherland.
FOUR! Finds the gap again! 10 runs off the over! Megan Schutt goes a bit too full this time, on off, Shafali Verma strides out and drills it hard between covers and extra covers for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Megan Schutt to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Fullish and around leg, Shafali Verma whips it away straight to square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Megan Schutt to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sees the batter back away and follows her, on a short of a length, Shafali Verma gets on her toes and tucks it to square leg. Smriti Mandhana wants a single but gets sent back by Shafali Verma.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Megan Schutt to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Intelligent batting! Megan Schutt bowls this on a hard length and around off, Shafali Verma takes a couple of steps forward, opens the face of the bat at the last moment to guide it past backward point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Megan Schutt to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and around off, Smriti Mandhana winds up to go big again, but punches it wide of extra covers for a run in the end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Megan Schutt to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, Shafali Verma drills it wide of cover-point where the fielder dives to her right to stop it. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Megan Schutt to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Smriti Mandhana goes big now! Annabel Sutherland pitches this one up, on off, in the slot as well, Smriti Mandhana clears her front leg away and hoicks it over the deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Annabel Sutherland to Smriti Mandhana, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: At 114.7 clicks, swinging in, on a length, on middle, Shafali Verma presses forward and nudges it to the right of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Annabel Sutherland to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Smriti Mandhana punches it through covers for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Annabel Sutherland to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes full this time, on the pads, Shafali Verma clips it wide of fine leg where Megan Schutt runs to her right and slides in to stop it. Only a run taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Annabel Sutherland to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jaffa! Annabel Sutherland lands this on a good length and on middle, nips back in a bit, Shafali Verma gets cut in half as the ball goes past the inside edge to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Annabel Sutherland to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller one and around off, angling away, Smriti Mandhana chases after it and carves it towards deep point for a single. That brings up 3000 runs for Smriti Mandhana in T20Is.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Annabel Sutherland to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! What a way to get off the mark! Megan Schutt overpitches it this time around off, Shafali Verma leans on nicely on to her drive and creams it from the middle of the bat through covers for a beautiful boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Megan Schutt to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: First runs off the bat! This is pitched up and on off, Smriti Mandhana heaves it off the inner half of the bat towards mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Megan Schutt to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Still no runs off the bat! Comes from around the wicket and bowls it on middle, Smriti Mandhana looks to drill this one down the ground but the bat twists in her hand and she mistimes it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Megan Schutt to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length delivery, swinging away, outside off, Smriti Mandhana opens her bat face and strokes it to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Megan Schutt to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls her length back and bowls it on off, Smriti Mandhana hangs back in her crease and steers it towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Megan Schutt to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and swinging away, on off, Smriti Mandhana drives it crisply but straight to extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Megan Schutt to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Megan Schutt.

On a length and around leg, Smriti Mandhana once again fails to get bat on ball as the ball goes off her pads towards square leg. A leg bye is taken. India Women have 14 runs on the board but none from the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller delivery and around off, Smriti Mandhana steers it towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: NO BALL AND FOUR! Things get even worse for Darcie Brown! She bowls this back of a length but way down the leg side, shaping in, Smriti Mandhana is nowhere near it to play, and Alyssa Healy also has no chance of stopping that as the ball goes to the fine leg fence again for a boundary. Initially, it is called five wides, but the replays show that Brown has overstepped. It is signalled a No ball and Free Hit will follow now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, No ball and 4 Byes.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES AGAIN! Similar delivery, similar result! Darcie Brown serves this one a touch fuller, but on the pads again, Smriti Mandhana misses her glance once again as the ball deflects off her pads to the fine leg fence for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! India Women are underway with extras! Darcie Brown errs in her line and lands this on a good length, but down the leg side, Smriti Mandhana looks to flick it away but misses, the ball goes off her pads and races to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and well outside off, shaping further away, Smriti Mandhana winds up for the pull but lets it go to the keeper in the end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Darcie Brown starts with a hard-length delivery, outside off, angling away, Smriti Mandhana loosely tries to cut it away without much footwork and misses it completely.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Darcie Brown to Smriti Mandhana, No run.
